4. By O2, at equilibrium, the probability of a state is proportional to \( e^{-E/k_BT} \). [O2]
5. Since the exponential function is strictly decreasing in \( E \), the inequality \( E_{	ext{native}} &lt; E_{	ext{non-native}}^{(i)} \) implies \( e^{-E_{	ext{native}}/k_BT} &gt; e^{-E_{	ext{non-native}}^{(i)}/k_BT} \) for each \( i \). [O2]
6. Therefore, the probability of the native state is greater than the probability of any single, specific non-native state at equilibrium. [O1, S1, O2]
